newsitem.title: USA: Neighboring utilities send power to NY after fire.
newsitem.headline: Neighboring utilities send power to NY after fire.

text.p: Utilities surrounding New York were pushing additional power into the city to help Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc (ConEd) cope with a crippling fire at one of its substations, utility officials said Wednesday.
Power companies connected to ConEd's system were moving at least 950 megawatts (MW) of power to the New York Power Pool to close the gap left by the outage.

"We're providing them with electricity. We are sending 600 megawatts to the pool," said a company spokesman for Public Service Electric and Gas Co (PSE&G), a subsidiary of Public Service Enterprise Group Inc in New Jersey.
A spokeswoman for the Long Island Lighting Co confirmed they were sending about 350 MW to the pool, which oversees the flow of power throughout the region.
The fire early Wednesday at ConEd's Sprain Brook facility, near Yonkers, was blamed for a major power dip in New York City, Westchester County and on Long Island.
It also shut six high-voltage transmission lines serving the area, restricting the flow of power from northern to southern New York state.

The PSE&G spokesman said the company was honoring a pact among the region's utilities to assist one another during emergencies to insure deliveries to customers and reliability of the transmission grid.
It was still unclear how long the Sprain Brook substation would be shut following the fire.
